body:
@emilio or @zcorpan, would you like to take an initial look?
This is ready including tests etc.

<details><summary>AI review</summary>

Reviewed at bf1fcc8 (with whatwg/dom#1512 at 4b91bf1 and web-platform-tests/wpt#63595 at 67961fc)

**Blockers**

- `source:114812-114813`: removing the document from *pending focus reset documents* in *destroy a document* never takes effect in time. *destroy a document and its descendants* runs in parallel and destroys in a queued task, so the mutation observer microtask always runs first. With `button.focus(); button.remove(); iframe.remove();` in a child document, the spec fires `focusreset` at both the child and the parent documents. `focusreset-iframe.html:266-288` expects only the parent. Consider removing the active document and its descendants' documents synchronously in *destroy a child navigable*, or re-checking at fire time (e.g. a hook so HTML can skip documents that no longer have focus).
- `focusreset-timing.html:15-36`, `focusreset-cancelled-by-focus-update.html:72-85`: these tests assume the mutation observer microtask is queued at removal time. But *queue a mutation record* always queues it, even with no observers. Setup earlier in the same microtask (`createFocusable()` sets `textContent` and calls `append()`) has already queued it, so *signal a focus reset* doesn't queue a new one. Per spec, `focusreset` fires before the microtask queued "before removal", and the "cancels focusreset" test gets one event, not zero. I think engines only queue it when something is observing, so this PR may make the gap observable. Either finish the setup in an earlier microtask (e.g. `await Promise.resolve()` before `queueMicrotask()`), or confirm in whatwg/dom#1512 which behavior is wanted and align the spec.

**Suggestions**

- `source:1853`, `source:1858-1864`: the note says that if *document* doesn't have focus, *removedNode* already got `blur`. That doesn't hold when the top-level traversable lacks system focus. Calling `el.focus()` in a background window runs the focus update steps with an empty old chain: `focus` fires, and nothing in the spec fires `blur` when system focus leaves. If *el* is then removed, it gets neither `blur` nor `focusreset`, so a focus trap never finds out. Either check only that *document* is in its top-level traversable's focus path, ignoring system focus, or confirm skipping is intended and fix the note.
- `support/focusreset-helpers.js:30`: every positive test needs system focus, because the *has focus steps* check is false without it. A runner whose window isn't focused fails them all with "expected 1, got 0". Consider asserting `document.hasFocus()` in `settle()` so the failure is clear.
- Test coverage: the cancellation tests only move focus with `focus()`/`blur()`. Consider adding:
  - another caller of the focusing steps, e.g. `dialog.showModal()` or `autofocus`;
  - a cross-origin iframe, since *pending focus reset documents* is per agent but the focus update steps remove across agents;
  - two documents reset in the same task, to check firing order.
- web-platform-tests/wpt#63595: `sanitizer-api/sanitizer-no-speculative-fetch.html` is unrelated and came in with "Mark focusreset tests as non-tentative". Consider dropping it.
- Naming: `NavigateEvent.intercept()` already has a `focusReset` option. A focus reset from it runs the focusing steps, so it fires `blur`/`focus` and not `focusreset`. Developers might expect `focusreset` there. Maybe worth checking whether the name overlap is OK.

**Nits**

- `source:123859-123863`: "it causes a `focusreset` event to be fired" overstates things, since it's skipped without focus or when focus is moved explicitly. Consider "it can cause".
- `source:87267-87268`: *documents* can hold duplicates. Consider "a set of".
- `source:162005-162009`: HTML's events index doesn't list other DOM-defined events (`slotchange` isn't there). Either drop the row, or keep it and add "while it has focus" to match the condition.
- `focusreset-basic.html:4-5` (and the other test files): `rel="help"` points at the PR and at `#focus-fixup-rule`, the rendering-step fixup, which doesn't fire `focusreset`. Consider `#node-remove-focus-fixup` and the DOM anchors.

</details>

> AI review

Addressed in the latest commits across HTML, DOM (whatwg/dom#1512), and WPT:
1. **Iframe removal after child removal (`button.focus(); button.remove(); iframe.remove()`):** Good catch — *destroy a document and its descendants* queues a task in parallel, so it never runs before the mutation observer microtask.
   - In DOM, *notify mutation observers* now re-checks a new exported hook, **focus reset relevance steps** (defaulting to `true`), before firing `focusreset`.
   - HTML overrides **focus reset relevance steps** to return the result of the **has focus steps** given *document*, and drops the unreachable cleanup step from *destroy a document*.
   - When the iframe is removed in the same task, only the parent document still has focus at the microtask checkpoint, so `focusreset` fires only on the parent (and at most one document per top-level traversable can fire in a given checkpoint, so cross-document firing order is no longer observable).
2. **MutationObserver microtask timing in WPT (`focusreset-timing.html`, `focusreset-iframe.html`):** No change needed here — DOM's *queue a mutation record* returns early before *queue a mutation observer microtask* when *interestedObservers* is empty (since whatwg/dom@3071e5f), so DOM setup prior to `observer.observe(...)` does not queue a mutation observer microtask. Added `assert_true(document.hasFocus())` in `settle()` so missing system focus fails with a clear precondition message.
3. **Note on *node-remove focus fixup* & system focus:** Keeping the *has focus steps* check is intentional (removals in background tabs/windows should not fire `focusreset`). Rewrote the note so it accurately reflects the *has focus steps* condition (including detached navigable containers and unfocused top-level traversables) and doesn't claim a `blur` event was already fired.
4. **Naming (`focusreset` vs. navigation API focus reset):** Keeping `focusreset`; added a note pointing to *potentially reset the focus* explaining that navigation focus reset runs the focusing steps (firing `blur`/`focus` as appropriate) and therefore counts as an explicit focus move rather than firing `focusreset`.
5. **Additional WPT coverage & spec cleanups:**
   - Added tests for `<dialog>` (`show()`/`showModal()`/`close()`), popovers (`showPopover()`/`hidePopover()`), cross-origin iframes (with `allow="focus-without-user-activation"`), and `document.open()`.
   - Changed *documents* to a set in *focus update steps* (we kept the `Element` or `Document` check since focus chains can also contain focusable regions/shapes), updated the event-loop note to say "can cause", alphabetized `onfocusreset` in `GlobalEventHandlers`, removed the `focusreset` row from the HTML events index (since it is defined in DOM), and updated `rel="help"` links.
Why does this need to happen at the end of current micro-task? Can't we just do it during the update-the-rendering step?

> Why does this need to happen at the end of current micro-task? Can't we just do it during the update-the-rendering step?

I originally prototyped it like that but the problem is that any js call in the update the rendering step can cause a focusreset by removing nodes. The only place to put it where that wouldn't cause an un-synced render is in the resize observer loop and that seems worse than aligning it with mutation observers and slotchange. 

In general I think results of mutations like this one should be mutation observer aligned.

But we can consider the other model as well.

> I originally prototyped it like that but the problem is that any js call in the update the rendering step can cause a focusreset by removing nodes. The only place to put it where that wouldn't cause an un-synced render is in the resize observer loop and that seems worse than aligning it with mutation observers and slotchange.

We have a focus fixup step 17 in [update the rendering](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#update-the-rendering). Why don't we fire this event there then?

> We have a focus fixup step 17 in [update the rendering](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#update-the-rendering). Why don't we fire this event there then?

Step 17 ([#focus-fixup-rule](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-fixup-rule)) is for when the focused element stops being a focusable area due to a rendering/style change (e.g., becoming `display: none`). It runs after the style/layout/`ResizeObserver` loop because the UA only knows the element stopped being rendered/focusable after updating style and layout. During this time, `document.activeElement` remains "dangling" on an element that might be unfocusable. OTOH, and importantly - the focus fixup updates `document.activeElement` and fires `blur` *together*.

When a focused element is removed from the DOM ([#node-remove-focus-fixup](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/infrastructure.html#node-remove-focus-fixup)), `document.activeElement` is **already reset synchronously during the DOM removal** (closer to an explicit `blur()`), not at step 17.
If we waited until step 17 to fire `focusreset`, we'd have quite a wait where `document.activeElement` and the fired events are out of sync.

Firing `focusreset` in the `MutationObserver` microtask keeps it coupled to the synchronous `activeElement` reset, only deferring to the end of the microtask so compound DOM mutations (like moving a node or replacing a list) settle first.
